four more secondary/tertiary "intvw book format" recs:

1. Drobny - "Inside The House of Money" (first photo)

intvw list just isn't as good as the top 4, and it overindexes way too heavily towards global macro.

[I can't find the sequel - "New House of Money" - intvw list anywhere...not sure why.]

2. Harriman House Book of Investing Rules

this is a 500-page book where each investor gets a 5-page top 10. many names you've never heard of, many you have: Dalio, Bogle, Gross, Faber, Grantham, Malkiel, Mauboussin, Niederhoffer

I recall there being lots of tidbits in there and it being worth the time, you learn a lot from the "non-household names."

3. Stock Market Wizards

this is 3rd after "new market wizards" I believe...I don't recognize many of the names ex. DE Shaw/SAC, but that doesn't mean they aren't worth the time.

[Schwager chronological order was:
1989: Market Wizards
1992: New Market Wizards
2001: Stock Market Wizards]

and then...

4. Hedge Fund Market Wizards (2012)

same idea as #3, although better intvw list...Platt in particular = "pit wisdom"

few others in there prob worth the time

it's Schwager so its never going to be bad

idk what came after this one, I think we're at "Substack Thinkboi Wizards" (2025) or "Wizards of SeekingAlpha" or some shit

--

overall, I won't pound the table on any of these like the Big Four, but all belong in a top 15 or top 20 "intvw format" context.
